view: This print has had most of its information taken out in advance. The quarter's comps went out on Nov 2 and drew a shrug. The refranchising arithmetic went out on Sept 1 and took about 23% off the stock in two weeks. What is left is the reframing: a new FY26 EBITDA outlook that will mechanically come in well below the $70-73M still on the books. My rough rebuild is high-$50s to low-$60s, from about 17 weeks without the sold units at ~$0.78M a week, partly offset by Q3 comps running well above the guide. Alongside it comes some first word on the run-rate of the franchised model (G&A, capex, interest now ~7% on $90M against ~12% on $167M), Q4-to-date comps against an easy base (Q4 2025 was guided to about -3%), and a clean 10-Q after the NT filing. There are two plausible headline readings. One is a 'guidance cut' read by thin coverage and algorithms, made worse by casual-dining traffic softening late in Q3 (Texas Roadhouse) and by a possible activist overhang. The other is 'underlying beat plus raise ex-refranchising, deleveraged, delay resolved', helped by a ~10% short base and a stock that has slid into the print. I cannot show which framing management will choose, or what the few analysts' FY26 numbers already include. So the direction is close to a coin flip with a slight lean up, from the slide into the print, short positioning and the strong comps two-year stack. The move should be large because the name is thin and short-heavy, but smaller than the options' 16% because the comps are already out.

recommendation.reason: The two facts that could have surprised, Q3 comps and the refranchising dilution, were published before today and the price visibly reacted to the second. What remains is how management frames the reset FY26 outlook and Q4-to-date trends, and no public trace I found tells me which way that lands against stale, thin consensus. No mechanism clears 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: If the release gives an updated FY26 adjusted EBITDA at or above ~$62M with Q4-to-date comps of +4% or better and a filed 10-Q with no material weakness, the short base would likely drive a large up move. A guide in the low-$50s or a disclosed control deficiency points the other way.

self_critique: The case for a confident short: thin coverage may still carry the stale $70-73M FY26 EBITDA, so the updated guide reads as a 15-20% cut. Last year's identical sequence (pre-release, then full results on 2025-11-10) drew -6.4%. Peer traffic weakened into Q4, and two freed activists holding ~19% have a reason to sell into any pop. The case for a long: three straight full prints moved +18% to +33%, ~10% of shares are short, the stock has given back 13% with no news, and an underlying beat ex-refranchising plus a clean 10-Q would surprise. Both are plausible and neither has a dated trace that settles it, so I stay near 50.
approach_notes: P4 ('priced in is a claim to prove') paid off. Reading the Article 11 pro formas and tying them to the September price drop showed the dilution was priced, rather than assuming it either way. P3's 'freshest data first' found little here because the company had already pre-released the fresh data, and the playbook gives no guidance on prints whose main datapoint is pre-announced.
